title: Surface circumferential spinal cord recording in freely moving rodents
directly_supported: Short-term spinal recordings: 15 rats overall; motor decoding subset 5; acute pigs 3.
not_established: Causal human online intent decoding; transferable expert skill; organ control.
scope_notes: Publisher full text verified. Intradural rat wrapping after durotomy. Pooled bidirectional decoder. Sensory/visceral experiments are input discrimination. Source's uniform-eight-class baseline wording needs clarification.

title: A Hyperflexible Electrode Array for Long-Term Recording and Decoding of Intraspinal Neuronal Activity
directly_supported: Penetrating ventral-horn recording over nine weeks in 5 mice; wheel-running decoding in 2 mice.
not_established: Chronic human performance; healthy skill transfer; fine finger specificity.
scope_notes: Publisher full text verified. Recording cohort L1-L2 spinal segments; decoding experiment L3 ventral horn. Separate experiments and sample sizes; channel counts are not animal counts.

title: Flexible circumferential bioelectronics to enable 360-degree recording and stimulation of the spinal cord
directly_supported: Rat recording/stimulation and acute spinal bypass; 16 acute rats; separate 6 passive dummy implants up to six weeks; human cadaver placement.
not_established: Chronic active human recording; physiological automation; retained expert skill transfer.
scope_notes: Primary full-text XML verified via Europe PMC; PMC browser challenge. Rat methods specify circumferential epidural access; human cadaver method uses durotomy/intradural passage. Dummy tissue-response testing is not active recording. No total cadaver count inferred.

title: A computational model for epidural electrical stimulation of spinal sensorimotor circuits
directly_supported: Rat field/axon models and in vivo experiments support afferent recruitment and trans-synaptic motor-circuit engagement in the tested EES setting.
not_established: Universal direct motoneuron activation; arbitrary selective inhibition; expert-voltage replay.
scope_notes: Author abstract verified via Europe PMC PMID 24305828. Publisher unavailable. Detailed cohort counts and parameter tables not verified here. Rat lumbosacral segments; no human vertebral placement inferred.

title: Spinal cord stimulation for upper limb motor function in people with chronic post-stroke hemiparesis: a feasibility trial
directly_supported: Seven implanted participants; four-week cervical stimulation feasibility; immediate arm assistance and stimulation-off clinical changes. Finger responses in 3/7 with residual connectivity.
not_established: Healthy piano acquisition; independent control of every finger; expert-driven learning acceleration.
scope_notes: Author abstract and figure captions verified via PubMed 42243548; publisher fetch failed. Two unilateral epidural leads and external stimulator. Figure examples C6/C7 label spinal segments; not identically numbered vertebrae. Small preliminary clinical study.

title: Activity-dependent spinal cord neuromodulation rapidly restores trunk and leg motor functions after complete paralysis
directly_supported: Activity-specific trunk/leg EES programs in 3 people with complete sensorimotor paralysis; personalized anatomy/recruitment-informed paddle design.
not_established: Healthy athletic enhancement; expert neural transfer; one stimulation pattern for all motor activities.
scope_notes: Publisher full text/extended-data verified. Distinguishes lumbosacral spinal segments and root targets from surgical placement. Imaging/model cohorts of 15 volunteers or 27 cords are not the 3 treated participants.

title: Targeted neurotechnology restores walking in humans with spinal cord injury
directly_supported: Three SCI participants; spatiotemporal stimulation supports walking; rehabilitation-related voluntary control without stimulation reported.
not_established: Expert-to-novice footwork transfer; a healthy learning-speed multiplier; all gait improvement persisting without assistance.
scope_notes: Publisher abstract and accessible extended-data/video captions verified. Full main article subscription-limited. SCI restoration and unassisted voluntary control endpoints differ from learning a new athletic skill.

title: Targeted, activity-dependent spinal stimulation produces long-lasting motor recovery in chronic cervical spinal cord injury
directly_supported: Rat EMG-triggered intraspinal stimulation with retraining; groups 9 activity-dependent/6 open-loop/9 retraining-only; benefit maintained three weeks without stimulation.
not_established: Spinal-recording trigger; direct demonstration of synaptic STDP mechanism; healthy expert skill transfer or 2x novice acquisition.
scope_notes: Author abstract via Europe PMC PMID 26371306 and primary PMC indexed methods/discussion verified. Direct PMC/browser/full XML fetch failed; unexamined detailed methods not asserted. Cervical contusion with spared pathways; intraspinal access differs from EES.

title: Spike-timing-dependent plasticity in primate corticospinal connections induced during free behavior
directly_supported: Cortical-spike-triggered intraspinal stimulation modified corticospinal connection strength in 2 monkeys; 19 conditioning sessions and 15 cell/site pairs.
not_established: Spinal-only recording architecture; expert imitation; retained human complex-skill transfer.
scope_notes: Author-hosted full manuscript verified at depts.washington.edu/fetzweb/assets/nishimura_neuron.pdf. Cortical recording plus cervical stimulation is hybrid access. Timing changed polarity; many effects eventually reverted. Session/cell counts are not animal counts.

title: Operant conditioning of a spinal reflex can improve locomotion after spinal cord injury in humans
directly_supported: 13 SCI participants: 9 down-conditioning and 4 measurement controls; 6/9 conditioned successfully over 30 sessions with persistent reflex changes and locomotor improvements.
not_established: Implanted spinal recording/stimulation; direct expert-to-learner transfer; universal response.
scope_notes: Author full manuscript verified at neurotechcenter.org. Tibial nerve surface stimulation and EMG evoke/measure soleus H-reflex. Evidence about conditioning a spinal pathway via peripheral access; not an invasive SCCI demonstration.

title: Electrical spinal cord stimulation must preserve proprioception to enable locomotion in humans with spinal cord injury
directly_supported: Computational/preclinical/clinical observations support stimulation-related disruption of proprioception and the importance of temporal patterns preserving afferent information.
not_established: Every stimulation protocol harms perception; healthy consumer efficacy; freely available sensory channels without interference.
scope_notes: Author abstract verified via Europe PMC PMID 30382196; publisher fetch failed in this audit. Rat-human differences matter. Individual experiment counts and detailed waveform values not verified here.

title: An implantable system to restore hemodynamic stability after spinal cord injury
directly_supported: Four trials with 14 implanted SCI participants; lower-thoracic targeted EES produces pressor responses; external-pressure feedback regulates systolic pressure.
not_established: Neural pressure decoding; active arbitrary pressure lowering; healthy enhancement; universal autonomic control.
scope_notes: Publisher full text verified. Head-to-head completed subset n=5; closed-loop figure subsets 3/4 and 2/3; not all 14. Last three thoracic SPINAL segments; example T11 vs L4. Imaging maps them to vertebral/surgical positions. Survey 1479 is separate.

title: Neuroprosthetic baroreflex controls haemodynamics after spinal cord injury
directly_supported: Preclinical and human proof of concept for feedback-controlled haemodynamic regulation after SCI using EES.
not_established: Full autonomic read/write; conscious arbitrary cardiovascular control; healthy-user benefit.
scope_notes: Publisher author abstract and extended-data human control diagram verified; main text subscription-limited. Rodents/nonhuman primates/humans are distinct cohorts. Overall cohort counts not independently verified in this audit; do not infer them from later 2025 trial.

title: A Pilot Feasibility Trial of Multi-Program Epidural Spinal Cord Stimulation for Bladder Function Recovery in Chronic Spinal Cord Injury
directly_supported: Four consented/3 implanted SCI participants; 2 completed 12-month follow-up. Personalized storage/voiding programs and training; high voiding efficiency achieved by one participant.
not_established: Autonomous neural fullness decoder; universal emptying; unlimited storage delay; equivalent benefit in healthy users.
scope_notes: Primary full-text XML verified via Europe PMC PMC 13513323; publisher 429. Lumbosacral SPINAL segments; placement mapped by anatomy and motor responses. Home user switched programs; bowel/sexual observations secondary. Benefit differs between catheterized cystometry and uroflow.

title: Lower thoracic spinal cord stimulation to restore cough in patients with spinal cord injury: results of a National Institutes of Health-sponsored clinical trial. Part I: methodology and effectiveness of expiratory muscle activation
directly_supported: Nine cervical-SCI participants with weak cough; implanted stimulation generates expiratory pressure and airflow relevant to cough.
not_established: Autonomous inspiration/ventilation; gas-exchange regulation; indefinite repetitive output without recovery.
scope_notes: Author abstract verified via Europe PMC PMID 19406289; PMC browser challenge/full XML unavailable. Abstract reports T9/T11/L1 'spinal levels'; no independent conversion to neural segments asserted. Do not interpret placement labels as proof of specific segment recruitment.

title: Sensory restoration by epidural stimulation of the lateral spinal cord in upper-limb amputees
directly_supported: Four upper-limb amputees experienced missing-limb sensory percepts with lateral cervical epidural stimulation; locations/intensities characterized over temporary implantation.
not_established: Pure motor-intent recording; naturalistic sensation on every contact; full-sensory virtual reality; healthy expert-learning benefit.
scope_notes: Primary full-text XML verified via Europe PMC PMC 7373432; eLife browser challenge. Often paresthetic percepts; some naturalistic reports. Three leads per person are not three participants. Peripheral nerve evidence discussed in article is distinct access.

title: Closed-loop stimulation of lateral cervical spinal cord in upper-limb amputees to enable sensory discrimination: a case study
directly_supported: Two upper-limb amputees used sensor-linked spinal sensory feedback for selected size/compliance discrimination tasks.
not_established: One-participant result; expert skill transfer; general sensory substitution benefit across all tasks.
scope_notes: Primary full-text XML verified via Europe PMC PMC 9553970 and publisher abstract. Lateral C5-C8 SPINAL cord/epidural lead description. Task success differed by person and property. 'Case study' does not imply n=1.

title: Epidural spinal cord stimulation can facilitate ejaculatory response in spinal cord injury individuals: a report of two cases
directly_supported: Two male chronic SCI cases report facilitation of ejaculation under epidural stimulation; additional stimulation such as penile vibration used.
not_established: Selective electrical delay; sustained orgasm; universal reproductive recovery; causal healthy-user enhancement.
scope_notes: Author abstract verified via Europe PMC PMID 37878354. Online 2023; issue 2024. Injury T4 is neurological injury level; it is not an electrode placement specification. Full stimulation-coordinate/parameter details not verified here.

title: Effect of epidural spinal cord stimulation on female sexual function after spinal cord injury
directly_supported: Secondary case-series analysis of 3 women with thoracic complete SCI; sexual-function/distress questionnaire changes during long-term ESCS.
not_established: Objective control of arousal duration; automatic onset/termination; prolonged subjective pleasure; healthy-user transfer.
scope_notes: Publisher full text verified. Questionnaire outcomes distinguish self-report from measured physiological state control. Small uncontrolled secondary analysis; does not identify a universally controllable sexual-state variable.

title: Ejaculation elicited by microstimulation of lumbar spinothalamic neurons
directly_supported: Microstimulation of lumbar LSt area elicited ejaculation sequence in=17 anaesthetized rats. Pharmacological inhibition interrupted contractions in a separate reported subset.
not_established: Human selective electrical inhibition or delay; cortical orgasm/pleasure control; chronic safe repeatability.
scope_notes: Author abstract verified via Europe PMC PMID 18394782. L4 refers to RAT spinal segment. Chemical muscimol interruption n=5 is not evidence that the same electrical interface provides an inhibitory channel.

title: Effects of physical guidance and knowledge of results on motor learning: support for the guidance hypothesis
directly_supported: In a human target-movement task guidance type/frequency affected retention and transfer; high-frequency physical guidance gave poorest retention.
not_established: A universal rule for every complex skill; spinal stimulation mechanism; proof SCCI_RH assistance will harm learning.
scope_notes: Author abstract verified via PubMed/Europe PMC PMID 7886280. Peripheral behavioral guidance comparator. Full article/cohort count not verified; no count invented. Motivates testing dependence rather than hardcoding favorable plasticity.

title: Walking naturally after spinal cord injury using a brain-spine interface
directly_supported: One SCI participant; cortical recording controls spinal EES; supported mobility and rehabilitation-related unassisted walking reported.
not_established: Spinal-only intent acquisition; expert skill transfer; direct novice acquisition multiplier.
scope_notes: Author abstract verified via Europe PMC PMID 37225984. Explicit hybrid brain-spine system; implanted cortical recording and spinal stimulation are separate access sites. Switching-off outcome is rehabilitation recovery in this participant.

title: Transcutaneous Spinal Cord Stimulation Disrupts Conscious Ankle Proprioception and Produces a More Constrained Locomotor Pattern in Unimpaired Adults
directly_supported: Preprint: 14 stimulated unimpaired adults plus 14 independent controls; acute proprioceptive disruption and subsequent adaptation reported.
not_established: Peer-reviewed evidence; invasive SCCI efficacy; expert-informed learning; equivalence of access modes.
scope_notes: Author preprint abstract/version=1 verified; submitted 2026-08-06. Transcutaneous access. Mixed immediate/adaptation outcomes motivate contrary tests; main statistical analysis not independently reanalyzed.

title: Effects of Lower Thoracic Spinal Cord Stimulation on Bowel Management in Individuals With Spinal Cord Injury
directly_supported: Five cervical-SCI participants using implanted cough system; bowel routine improvement attributed to restored intra-abdominal pressure development.
not_established: Direct enteric-state decoding; fully coordinated bowel automation; arbitrary continence delay.
scope_notes: Author abstract verified via Europe PMC PMID 33161007; PMC browser challenge. Online 2020/issue 2021. Pressure/expulsive assistance and routine logs differ from direct sacral/enteric transition control.

title: Long-term safety and efficacy of closed-loop spinal cord stimulation to treat chronic back and leg pain (Evoke): a double-blind, randomised, controlled trial
directly_supported: 134 randomized (67/arm); ECAP-controlled versus fixed-output stimulation; reported clinical pain outcomes favored closed-loop in the tested population.
not_established: ECAP as a direct pain/intent readout; universal pain elimination; expert-learning effect.
scope_notes: Author abstract verified via PubMed 31870766. Online 2019/issue 2020. Analysed 125 at 3 months and 118 at 12 months; those are not new cohorts. Comparator is active open-loop stimulation, not placebo.

title: Effect of Spinal Cord Burst Stimulation vs Placebo Stimulation on Disability in Patients With Chronic Radicular Pain After Lumbar Spine Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial
directly_supported: 50 randomized; 42 completed all periods; placebo-controlled crossover found no significant disability benefit of the tested burst stimulation.
not_established: Failure of all spinal stimulation waveforms; absence of every physiological effect; motor-learning outcome.
scope_notes: Author abstract verified via Europe PMC PMID 36255427. Specific postsurgical radicular-pain population/waveform. Do not pool with ECAP-controlled active-comparator trial as the same question.
